narrative:
The model estimates a 73% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional profile that strongly signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

Your total years of experience across all jobs ranks as the most influential factor. At 6-10 years, this places you in a mid-career stage where many employees begin exploring new opportunities, pushing the prediction noticeably toward leaving. Second, the time you have spent in your current role—1 to 5 years—also contributes to the decision in the same direction. Employees predicted to stay tend to have either much shorter or significantly longer tenure here, making your current duration a moderate risk indicator.

Finally, having received other job offers while employed here is the third strongest driver, further increasing the likelihood of departure. This combination suggests the model sees you as someone with enough experience to be marketable, yet not so rooted in this organization that you are likely to remain long-term.

The company should consider discussing retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths or enhanced recognition. You may wish to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your career goals. Addressing these areas could help reduce the risk of turnover. (218 words)
